annotations.title: Crimea Is Ukraine - United States Department of State

content.text:
**Under international law and the position of most countries: no — Crimea does not belong to Russia; it is recognized as part of Ukraine.**

Russia has **controlled Crimea since 2014** after invading/occupying it and then claiming to annex it following a disputed referendum. But the **UN General Assembly affirmed Ukraine’s territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders** and said the referendum had no validity as a basis for changing Crimea’s status. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly_Resolution_68/262?utm_source=openai))

So the practical answer is:

- **De jure / legally internationally:** Crimea is **Ukraine**.
- **De facto / on the ground:** Crimea is **controlled by Russia**.
- **Russia’s position:** Crimea is part of the Russian Federation.
- **Ukraine, the U.S., EU, and most UN member states’ position:** Crimea is Ukrainian territory under Russian occupation. The U.S. State Department, for example, states that it does not recognize Russia’s annexation and considers Crimea part of Ukraine. ([2021-2025.state.gov](https://2021-2025.state.gov/crimea-is-ukraine/?utm_source=openai))
